help.title: About Stock transfers
help.overview: A stock transfer moves free stock from one warehouse to another. It stays a draft until it is completed or cancelled. Completing it is the moment the quantities actually move.

sections.title: The draft
sections.body: While it is a draft, nothing has left the source warehouse.
items: From warehouse and to warehouse are both required, and they are different warehouses.
Each line is a product, an optional variant, and a quantity.
You can still change a draft. Only a draft can be completed or cancelled.

sections.title: What complete does
sections.body: Complete is all or nothing. One short line refuses the whole transfer.
items: Every line leaves the source and arrives at the destination.
Only free stock moves. Units already reserved for open orders stay where they are.
If the destination has never stocked that item, the inventory row is created.
The ledger gets a transfer out on the source and a transfer in on the destination.

sections.title: After it is done
sections.body: A completed transfer is history. A cancelled draft never moved stock.
items: Cancel is only from draft, so a completed transfer is not undone from here.
The new on-hand numbers are on Inventory. The two movements are under Stock movements.
Deleting a transfer is a soft delete and it can be restored.
